data.title: TDS outlines $990M-$1.01B 2026 telecom revenue and $750M CapEx as fiber build accelerates
data.description:
Earnings Call Insights: Telephone and Data Systems (TDS) Q3 2026

Management View

  • "Over the past several years, we have taken many strategic actions that position us well both for today and the future. Those include exiting the wireless business, monetizing spectrum at attractive values, retaining tower assets that can benefit from future demand, investing in fiber without the burden of high leverage in a period of rising interest rates and repurchasing shares at prices we believe are attractive." (Chairman, President & CEO Walter C.D. Carlson)
  • "I do want to briefly comment on TDS' withdrawal of the previously announced offer to acquire the minority interest of Array in an all-stock transaction... the 2 parties were unable to reach agreement on value and form of consideration." (Chairman, President & CEO Carlson)
  • "TDS Telecom continues to advance its long-term goal of reaching 2.1 million marketable fiber service addresses, adding approximately 76,000 in the third quarter." (Executive VP, CFO & Director Vicki Villacrez)
  • "Following the termination of TDS' offer to acquire Array, we were in the market and have now virtually exhausted all of our prior share repurchase authorization of $520 million." (Executive VP, CFO & Director Villacrez)
  • "The TDS Board has approved an additional $250 million share repurchase authorization." (Executive VP, CFO & Director Villacrez)
  • "We completed the acquisition of Granite State Communications... that brings nearly 13,000 fully fibered service addresses to the portfolio, strengthening our Northeast fiber cluster." (Executive VP, CFO & Director Villacrez)
  • "We ended the third quarter with approximately 17,000 fiber net adds, our highest quarterly result in company history, up approximately 50% year-over-year." (President, CEO & Director Kenneth Dixon)
  • "Based on the information available today, we've refined our estimate to 1,200 to 1,600 tenantless towers." (President, CEO & Director Anthony Carlson)

Outlook

  • TDS Telecom guidance was revised to "total telecom revenues of $990 million to $1.01 billion" and "adjusted EBITDA guidance range downward to $290 million to $310 million," alongside CapEx now "approximately $750 million." (VP of Finance & CFO Kristina Bothfeld)
  • Bothfeld framed the demand/cost tradeoff behind the telecom changes: "We were anticipating fiber revenues to more than offset legacy declines during the second half of 2026, but continue to work toward that inflection point." (VP Bothfeld)
  • Array said, "our outlook remains unchanged," with expectations for "total operating revenue of $205 million to $215 million, adjusted OIBDA of $60 million to $75 million and adjusted EBITDA of $220 million to $235 million" and CapEx of "$25 million to $35 million." (President, CEO & Director Carlson)
  • No usable analysts’ estimates comparison was included because the provided estimates data did not present fiscal quarters in the required Q1–Q4 format and did not include EPS.

Financial Results

  • TDS Telecom reported Q3 dynamics of "Total operating revenues declined 3% in the quarter or 1% excluding the impact of divestitures" and "Cash expenses increased 4%," including "$4.2 million of strategic alternatives costs primarily related to workforce reductions." (VP Bothfeld)
  • Bothfeld cited profitability pressure: "The decline in adjusted EBITDA for the quarter reflects these cost pressures as well as top line headwinds from divestitures and legacy revenue streams." (VP Bothfeld)
  • Capital intensity rose with the fiber build: "Capital expenditures totaled $251 million in the quarter" driven by "a higher mix of buried versus aerial builds" and "a record level of addresses under construction." (VP Bothfeld)
  • On Array’s tower business, management highlighted revenue momentum but acknowledged mix shift as integration proceeds: "As T-Mobile continues its network integration activities, we are continuing to see the expected reduction in interim site revenue as those sites are terminated." (President, CEO & Director Carlson)

Q&A

  • Ric Prentiss, Raymond James: asked about stemming copper revenue declines and timing of a broader inflection; President Dixon answered, "this is core to our strategy is deploying fiber into those E-ACAM markets and then along the route, picking up those copper served addresses," and VP Bothfeld added, "that inflection point is around the corner. It's not years away." (President Dixon; VP Bothfeld)
  • Ric Prentiss, Raymond James: asked about OIBDA turning to growth; VP Bothfeld said, "we are on pace to hit our transformation initiatives" and "by year-end 2028, we'll deliver $100 million in run rate benefits." (VP Bothfeld)
  • Ric Prentiss, Raymond James: asked about DISH sites and satellite-driven tower opportunity; President Carlson said, "we had about 330 DISH sites" and later added, "if the number of major carriers goes from 3 to 4 or more... that means more revenue for us." (President Carlson)
  • Michael Rollins, Citigroup: asked about fixed wireless/satellite competition and ARPU; President Dixon responded, "where TDS has deployed fiber, we're not seeing a material impact from satellite" and tied demand to "our biggest fiber net add" and "double digits" usage growth year-over-year. (President Dixon)
  • Sergey Dluzhevskiy, GAMCO: asked what could revive a TDS-Array combination; Chairman Carlson said, "We don't comment on specific future plans" and "there may be circumstances where it makes sense to do this again." (Chairman Carlson)
  • Sergey Dluzhevskiy, GAMCO: pressed on build pace vs. go-to-market; President Dixon pointed to E-ACAM milestones and sales levers, including "driv[ing] more and more of our overall distribution to our lowest cost of acquisition channel, which is dot-com." (President Dixon)
  • Sergey Dluzhevskiy, GAMCO: asked for color on C-band monetization interest; President Carlson said, "We don't have any further specific update" and reiterated it is "a very attractive asset for C-band." (President Carlson)

Sentiment Analysis

  • Analysts: slightly negative, centered on legacy revenue erosion, timing of the telecom inflection, and visibility into spectrum/tower catalysts, including Prentiss’ focus on copper declines and Dluzhevskiy’s questions about a future TDS-Array combination.
  • Management: slightly positive in prepared remarks (record fiber execution; capital flexibility) and more measured in Q&A, with cautious phrasing around timing and transactions, including "we don't have any further specific update" on C-band and "We don't comment on specific future plans" on a renewed combination. (President Carlson; Chairman Carlson)
  • Versus Q2, Q3 tone shifted from transaction-process constraint to post-decision execution, after management disclosed the withdrawn Array minority offer and emphasized buybacks and operating targets.

Quarter-over-Quarter Comparison

  • The current call disclosed an outcome on the previously discussed Array minority proposal: Q2 said, "we will not be providing an update today" and "That process is ongoing" (Chairman, President & CEO Carlson), while Q3 said the offer was withdrawn because the parties "were unable to reach agreement on value and form of consideration." (Chairman, President & CEO Carlson)
  • Capital return messaging changed from being restricted in Q2 to active repurchases in Q3, with Villacrez saying buybacks were virtually completed under the prior $520 million authorization and a new $250 million authorization was approved.
  • TDS Telecom’s 2026 guidance moved lower on revenue and adjusted EBITDA and higher on CapEx in Q3, with Bothfeld explicitly linking the update to legacy pressures and accelerated construction activity.
  • Array’s tenantless tower estimate tightened to "1,200 to 1,600" in Q3 versus "1,000 to 1,700" in Q2, while Array’s stated outlook remained unchanged in Q3.

Risks and Concerns

  • Telecom profitability pressure remained tied to legacy declines and higher operating costs: "we are very bullish on our fiber growth future, but continue to see pressure on our legacy business" and cash expenses rose on expansion support and inflation. (President Dixon; VP Bothfeld)
  • Execution and cost risk within the fiber build was highlighted through higher construction complexity: "We are seeing higher costs to complete our E-ACAM builds in certain areas" and an increased use of "more costly construction techniques." (VP Bothfeld)
  • On Array, management emphasized integration and churn in interim revenues: "we are continuing to see the expected reduction in interim site revenue" as T-Mobile integration progresses, alongside multiyear work to address tenantless towers and ground leases. (President Carlson)

Final Takeaway

Management framed Q3 as a quarter of accelerated fiber build and customer adds alongside ongoing legacy revenue and cost pressures, while also marking a clear shift in capital allocation after withdrawing the Array minority acquisition proposal. TDS Telecom’s updated 2026 ranges lowered revenue and adjusted EBITDA expectations and raised CapEx to support record construction and an expanded pipeline, while Array reiterated an unchanged full-year outlook, refined the tenantless tower estimate, and maintained a disciplined stance on C-band monetization timing.

data.title: Alphabet’s drone unit to invest up to $125M in new manufacturing facility
data.description:
The drone division of Alphabet (GOOG) (GOOGL) called Wing, is investing up to $125 million over the next two years in a new manufacturing facility aimed at ramping up its delivery service across the U.S.

The 15,000-square-foot plant will be in Fort Worth, Texas, and would have the capacity to build tens of thousands of aircraft each year, the company said.

Wing is aiming to scale to nearly 20 U.S. markets by 2027 through its partnership with Walmart, up from a current footprint of five metropolitan areas, it added.

“Drone delivery has become a global reality, driven by clear demand from our partners and their customers,” said Adam Woodworth, CEO of Wing, adding that the U.S. is the company's focus for growth.

Wing began in 2012 as a Google (GOOG) (GOOGL) X “moonshot” project, conducting its first autonomous delivery tests in Australia in 2014. By 2018, it graduated into an independent Alphabet subsidiary. In 2019, Wing made aviation history as the first drone company to secure FAA Air Carrier Certification, launching America's first commercial home-delivery service in Virginia.

data.title: CareTrust projects 2026 normalized FFO per share of $2.08-$2.09 as LNT conversions to RIDEA are expected to begin in 2027
data.description:
Earnings Call Insights: CareTrust REIT (CTRE) Q3 2026

Management View

  • "Normalized FFO per share is up 20% over last year. And year-to-date, we've set another record of approximately $2.9 billion invested across all 3 growth engines, setting up 2027 to be another strong year of growth." (CEO, President & Director David Sedgwick)
  • "Now on October 1, we crossed the start line on a strategic relationship with LNT." (CEO, President & Director Sedgwick) "When the ramp-up phase flips from triple-net to SHOP, our first-year NOI yield will be in the high 7% range with a strong runway of growth from there to conservatively achieve our target of double-digit returns." (CEO, President & Director Sedgwick)
  • "In the third quarter alone, we closed approximately $740 million of investments at a blended stabilized yield of 8.3%." (CEO, President & Director Sedgwick) "Lease coverage set another record this quarter. Skilled nursing EBITDAR lease coverage hit 2.62x and EBITDARM of 3.26x across the stabilized portfolio, up again from last quarter." (CEO, President & Director Sedgwick)
  • "Taken together, our 2026 investments now stand at approximately $2.9 billion year-to-date at a blended yield of approximately 8.1%." (Chief Investment Officer & Secretary James Callister) "Our pipeline currently sits at just over $1.2 billion." (Chief Investment Officer & Secretary Callister)
  • "For the quarter, normalized FFO increased 37% over the prior year quarter to $129.2 million, and normalized FAD increased 36% to $127 million." (CFO & Treasurer Derek Bunker)

Outlook

  • "We're now projecting normalized FFO per share of $2.08 to $2.09, and normalized FAD per share of $2.04 to $2.05." (CFO & Treasurer Bunker)
  • "Our guidance is based on a weighted average diluted share count of 240 million shares" (CFO & Treasurer Bunker) and "includes the following key assumptions: first, no new investments, loans, or dispositions beyond those made or announced year-to-date; second, no new debt or equity issuances beyond those made year-to-date; third, 2.5% inflation-based rent escalators under our long-term triple-net leases; fourth, $147 million of loans to be repaid throughout the year, of which $111 million have been received so far to date; and fifth, no material change in the pound sterling to U.S. dollar spot exchange rate." (CFO & Treasurer Bunker)
  • "All else equal, if we were to utilize that capacity to fund the pipeline, by the end of 2027, we could be reporting another year of double-digit normalized FFO per share growth while keeping pro forma leverage still well below that range, all without accessing capital markets." (CFO & Treasurer Bunker)

Financial Results

  • "On a per-share basis, normalized FFO was $0.54" (CFO & Treasurer Bunker) and "normalized FAD was $0.53." (CFO & Treasurer Bunker)
  • "During the third quarter, we settled all of the 14.4 million shares outstanding under our May forward equity offering for gross proceeds of $578 million." (CFO & Treasurer Bunker) "We also issued 7 million shares under our ATM program at a weighted average price of $40.11 for gross proceeds of $280 million." (CFO & Treasurer Bunker)
  • "Subsequent to quarter end, we closed on a new $700 million unsecured term loan maturing in 2032, and we expanded our unsecured revolving credit facility to $2 billion." (CFO & Treasurer Bunker)
  • "As of today, [liquidity] stands at approximately $2.3 billion, including approximately $100 million of cash on hand, $1.6 billion of availability under our $2 billion revolving credit facility, and $599 million of capacity available under our ATM program." (CFO & Treasurer Bunker)

Q&A

  • Farrell Granath, BofA Securities: asked what makes LNT different and whether it’s replicable; CEO Sedgwick said, "LNT is really the most prolific developer of care homes in the U.K." and added, "on a programmatic way at scale, I think LNT is really one of one."
  • Farrell Granath, BofA Securities: asked about growth beyond the initial 45 homes; CEO Sedgwick said, "Ultimately, we decided that the more prudent approach would be to take this first step of doing an asset deal" and later added that acquiring all of LNT could become "self-evident."
  • Austin Wurschmidt, KeyBanc: asked about LNT pricing power; CEO Sedgwick said, "We believe that that's exactly what it does" and described targeting "that upper-middle class" with pricing "about 10% below that real high-end RevPOR."
  • Austin Wurschmidt, KeyBanc: asked for development and fee context; CIO Callister said, "Typical development we see in the U.K. runs about GBP 250,000 per unit" and added, "their average weekly fee is around GBP 1,500."
  • Robin Haneland, BMO (for Juan): asked about monetizing high SNF coverage via transitions/resets; CEO Sedgwick cited a tenant swap where a replacement operator "was willing to increase rent by 6%" and said, "we expect there to be more opportunities like that in coming years."
  • Vikram Malhotra, Mizuho: asked about yield upside on conversion; CFO Bunker said, "Assuming very modest growth, you're getting into the low 8% yields" and also said on U.K. tax, "we're able to probably capture or to protect about, call it, 1/4 of the leakage we're experiencing right now."
  • Michael Mueller, JPMorgan: asked if 2027 growth without capital markets is the plan; CFO Bunker said, "I think it was a little more of the latter, thought exercise" and added, "I wouldn't be surprised to see us continue to participate somewhat in other forms of capital."
  • Omotayo Okusanya, Deutsche Bank: questioned multiyear sustainability amid higher capital costs; CEO Sedgwick said, "one way to help predict the future is to build it" and added, "we're very confident that we're going to be able to continue to grow in a meaningful way."

Sentiment Analysis

  • Analyst tone was slightly negative to pressing on sustainability and valuation optics, including Deutsche Bank’s question highlighting "flat stock performance" and asking whether this is "a multiyear growth story rather than growth dramatically slowing in 2028."
  • Management tone was positive and confident, with CEO Sedgwick saying, "we are as bullish as ever" and CFO Bunker emphasizing, "our balance sheet is built for the identified and actionable opportunities ahead."
  • Compared with Q2, the current call spent more time defending durability of growth under rate volatility and explaining LNT structure, while Q2 leaned more on broad momentum, including "the CareTrust flywheel cranked up" and being "super bullish on the CareTrust story." (CEO, President & Director Sedgwick)

Quarter-over-quarter Comparison

  • Q3 foregrounded LNT as a new strategic growth engine, with CEO Sedgwick saying, "we crossed the start line on a strategic relationship with LNT," versus Q2’s emphasis on "3 growth engines" without LNT.
  • Guidance language shifted from Q2 "We're now projecting normalized FFO per share of $2.03 to $2.06" (CFO & Treasurer Bunker) to Q3 "We're now projecting normalized FFO per share of $2.08 to $2.09" (CFO & Treasurer Bunker), described as "raised the low end" after an October increase.
  • Investment pace messaging moved from Q2 "approximately $900 million of investments at a blended stabilized yield of 8.9%" (Chief Investment Officer & Secretary Callister) to Q3 "approximately $740 million" at "over 8.3%" (Chief Investment Officer & Secretary Callister), alongside Q3’s larger year-to-date total of "approximately $2.9 billion" (CEO, President & Director Sedgwick).
  • Balance sheet updates became more central in Q3, including "expanded our unsecured revolving credit facility to $2 billion" (CFO & Treasurer Bunker) versus Q2’s liquidity framework built around the prior revolver size and unsettled forwards.

Risks and Concerns

  • "Rates have certainly moved against everyone this fall." (CEO, President & Director Sedgwick) "In times of rising rates and uncertainty, sellers prioritize the buyer who will close, and that's us." (CEO, President & Director Sedgwick)
  • "You can't predict the future." (CEO, President & Director Sedgwick) "But one way to help predict the future is to build it." (CEO, President & Director Sedgwick)
  • "There's some leakage there that we can make some progress on" regarding U.K. taxes (CFO & Treasurer Bunker), alongside a timeline: "over the next 12 to 24 months." (CFO & Treasurer Bunker)

Final Takeaway

Management emphasized record year-to-date investment volume and record lease coverage, while positioning the LNT relationship as a differentiated pipeline into U.K. care homes and future SHOP/RIDEA economics. The company raised the low end of full-year 2026 per-share guidance and highlighted expanded bank capacity and liquidity as support for closing a stated pipeline while staying below its long-term leverage target range, with management repeatedly framing rising-rate volatility as a competitive opportunity for CareTrust’s funding certainty and deal execution.

data.title: Expensify signals $13.5M-$15.5M 2026 free cash flow guidance as New Expensify ARR tops $13M
data.description:
Earnings Call Insights: Expensify (EXFY) Q3 2026

Management View

  • "Revenue for the quarter was $33 million" and "Average paid members were 630,000" (CFO Ryan Schaffer).
  • "Operating cash flow was $4 million and free cash flow was $3.3 million" and "Our GAAP net loss was $3.3 million" (CFO Schaffer).
  • "Today, we're raising our full year 2026 free cash flow guidance of $12 million to $14 million, up to $13.5 million to $15.5 million" (CFO Schaffer).
  • "In Q3, we repurchased 722,121 shares of our Class A common stock for approximately $1.3 million" (CFO Schaffer).
  • "Revenue from New Expensify... grew 30% from Q2 and up 212% year-on-year to over $13 million in ARR" (Founder, CEO David Barrett).
  • "On reach, we're now issuing in pounds and euros, serving 13 European and U.K. markets" and "we've added enhanced PIN and biometric controls, one-time and date-bound virtual cards and 14 new rules that block out-of-policy purchases before they happen" (CEO Barrett).
  • "Trips booked through Expensify Travel grew 13% from Q2 and 40% year-over-year, and Q3 was the biggest quarter on record" and "we launched consolidated travel billing" (CEO Barrett).
  • "We launched native integrations with Rillet and DualEntry" and "in September, Expensify became one of the first expense tools in Anthropic's Claude for Small Business plug-in" (CEO Barrett).
  • "Earlier this week, we announced a referral agreement with Visa" and "Visa can now refer eligible clients and corporate card programs to Expensify" (CEO Barrett).
  • "Today, Expensify's agent handles over 96% of what it's asked to do without any constraints on what the user can ask" (CEO Barrett).

Outlook

  • "We're raising our full year 2026 free cash flow guidance... up to $13.5 million to $15.5 million" and "for October 2026, we had 636,000 paid members" (CFO Schaffer).
  • Compared with the prior quarter, management again raised full-year free cash flow guidance, moving from "up to $12 million to $14 million" (Q2) to "up to $13.5 million to $15.5 million" (Q3) (CFO Schaffer).

Financial Results

  • "Expensify Card interchange revenue across both Classic and New Expensify was $5.8 million, up 8% year-over-year" (CFO Schaffer).
  • "Non-GAAP net income was $3.1 million and adjusted EBITDA was $6.1 million" (CFO Schaffer).
  • "Q3 free cash flow was $3.3 million, which increased 170% from the same period last year" (CFO Schaffer).

Q&A

  • Mark Schappel, Loop Capital Markets LLC: asked whether Travel helps win new customers or mainly expands wallet share/retention; CEO Barrett replied, "the most important and urgent at the start was actually to reduce churn," while adding Travel also acts as "a major lead generator" and expansion lever; CFO Schaffer added, "Now we see -- we pull customers from Navan" and said consolidated travel billing has made Expensify "very competitive on price" (CEO Barrett; CFO Schaffer).
  • Mark Schappel, Loop Capital Markets LLC: asked about the Claude for Small Business bundle impact on acquisition/retention; CFO Schaffer responded, "it's very flattering to be picked by Anthropic," called it "a strong validation," and said, "we view this as a start of long-term partnership with Anthropic" (CFO Schaffer).
  • Aaron Kimson, Citizens JMP: asked for visibility into when New Expensify net new growth can outpace Classic attrition; CFO Schaffer said Expensify is "an exciting technology startup company hidden inside of our kind of legacy technology company" and added, "We think if things stay the same, that will happen next year"; CEO Barrett said, "even a relatively small decrease in churn can have a really rapid impact upon top line revenue growth" and "we feel confident" the tipping point is coming (CFO Schaffer; CEO Barrett).
  • Aaron Kimson, Citizens JMP: asked whether Expensify is seeing common traits among the targeted "99%" of businesses; CEO Barrett answered, "we've never really had a particular vertical alignment" and emphasized a strategy of meeting customers in their existing tools, noting "agents currently are able to do about 96% of what they're asked to do" and pointing to usage through "Claude" and "e-mail" (CEO Barrett).

Sentiment Analysis

  • Analysts: slightly positive, with questions oriented toward growth inflection timing and the practical impact of Travel and Anthropic; the tone included constructive framing such as "that's really helpful" and "really encouraging" (Aaron Kimson, Citizens JMP; Mark Schappel, Loop Capital Markets LLC).
  • Management: slightly positive in prepared remarks, with repeated momentum language including "adoption is exploding" and "the growth engine really started to show up in the numbers" (CEO David Barrett), while in Q&A management used more uncertainty language about timing such as "remains to be seen" (CFO Ryan Schaffer) and "it's hard to project when that tipping point will happen" (CEO Barrett).
  • Versus the prior quarter, management continued to frame the business as two opposing trajectories; Q3 added more timing specificity with "that will happen next year" (CFO Schaffer), while maintaining prior-quarter caution about forecasting precision.

Quarter-over-quarter Comparison

  • Q3 emphasized execution across multiple growth vectors at once: "New Expensify revenue, the Card, Travel, our partner ecosystem and our AI all moved forward at the same time" (CEO Barrett) versus Q2’s heavier emphasis on shipping velocity and AI feature expansion ("more than 30 features and enhancements") (CEO Barrett).
  • Free cash flow guidance was raised again quarter-over-quarter, from "up to $12 million to $14 million" (Q2) to "up to $13.5 million to $15.5 million" (Q3) (CFO Schaffer).
  • Capital return shifted from Q2’s large tender offer ("repurchasing approximately 6.1 million shares") to Q3’s smaller open-market activity ("repurchased 722,121 shares") (CFO Schaffer).
  • Travel messaging evolved from Q2 positioning around consolidated travel billing pipeline to Q3’s competitive narrative in Q&A, including "Now we're pulling customers from Navan" (CFO Schaffer).

Risks and Concerns

  • "While we continue to see some pressure on the top line" (CFO Ryan Schaffer).
  • "We have this quickly growing New Expensify platform, and then we have this large but slowly declining sort of legacy Classic customer base" and "it's hard to project when that tipping point will happen" (Founder, CEO David Barrett).
  • "We think if things stay the same, that will happen next year" but timing could move "earlier" or "later" depending on performance (CFO Schaffer).

Final Takeaway

Management framed Q3 around improving cash generation while accelerating New Expensify traction: CFO Ryan Schaffer reported $33 million of revenue, raised full-year 2026 free cash flow guidance to $13.5 million to $15.5 million, and highlighted share repurchases, while CEO David Barrett pointed to 30% sequential New Expensify net-new revenue growth to over $13 million in ARR, international Expensify Card expansion across 13 European and U.K. markets, record Travel volume, and expanded distribution via Anthropic’s Claude plug-in and a new Visa referral agreement, with Q&A attention centered on churn reduction and when New Expensify growth can outweigh Classic attrition.

data.title: Dream Office REIT outlines 2026 FFO guidance of $2.35-$2.40 per unit while resetting Toronto occupancy targets to 85%-87% after ILAC bankruptcy
data.description:
Earnings Call Insights: Dream Office Real Estate Investment Trust (D.UN:CA) Q3 2026

Management View

  • Chairman & CEO Michael J. Cooper described improving Canadian office fundamentals, saying, "the last 5 quarters have been really good for the office market in Canada, especially in Toronto," citing "reduction of sublease space, reduction of vacancy, increase of occupancy."
  • Cooper flagged ILAC’s collapse as the key negative development, stating, "The punch to the gut was finding out that ILAC had ceased operations," adding, "We had no expectation."
  • CFO Siu-Ming Lau highlighted market and portfolio leasing momentum, including: "National vacancy decreased by 40 basis points quarter-over-quarter to 16.7%," and "Downtown Toronto vacancy decreased by 90 basis points to 13.1% and experienced 709,000 square feet of positive absorption."
  • Lau detailed leasing volumes and the ILAC exposure: "Dream Office completed 43,000 square feet of new leases and 49,000 square feet of renewals," and "ILAC previously occupied 132,000 square feet across our Toronto portfolio."
  • Chief Financial Officer Jay Jiang emphasized that ILAC drove an occupancy target reset but not a change to FFO guidance, stating, "Despite the decline, we are still maintaining our 2026 FFO guidance of $2.35 to $2.40 per unit."

Outlook

  • Management lowered year-end Toronto occupancy targets following ILAC’s post-quarter-end lease disclaimer: "we are updating our year-end Toronto committed occupancy target to 85% to 87% and our in-place occupancy target to 82% to 84%" (CFO Siu-Ming Lau).
  • Lau kept NOI growth targets unchanged, stating, "we are maintaining our 2026 comparative properties NOI growth targets of 3% to 5% for Downtown Toronto and 1% to 3% for the total portfolio."
  • Jiang framed ILAC as a temporary earnings headwind beginning in Q4 2026, saying, "temporary revenue exposure of ILAC is approximately $4.3 million per year or just over $0.05 per unit of FFO starting in Q4."
  • No usable analyst EPS/revenue estimates comparison was possible because the provided estimates data did not include transcript-matching EPS/revenue figures and did not follow the required quarter formatting; management did not disclose quarterly revenue guidance in the call.

Financial Results

  • Jiang reported Q3 diluted FFO of $0.62 per unit, stating, "This compares to $0.65 per unit last quarter and $0.60 per unit in the third quarter of 2025."
  • Management cited operating performance gains in Toronto and the broader portfolio: "comparative properties NOI increased by 4.5% year-over-year to $24.4 million" and "For Toronto, comparative property NOI increased by 4.1% year-over-year to $20.3 million" (CFO Siu-Ming Lau).
  • Jiang said straight-line rent remained elevated: "straight-line rent remained strong at $2.1 million this quarter," and added, "we expect to see this trend continue in Q4 and into 2027" as leases commence.
  • Jiang characterized operating leverage improvements: "Excluding bad debt provision, our NOI margin this quarter was about 55%, up roughly 130 basis points from the same quarter last year."
  • Jiang reported valuation and balance-sheet items, including: "Our net asset value per unit was $48.64, down $0.59 or 1.2% from last quarter," and "We ended the quarter with about $102 million of cash and undrawn revolver capacity."

Q&A

  • Sairam Srinivas, ATB Cormark: asked how to frame ILAC in 2027; CFO Jiang said, "We quantified the impact of ILAC simply, which is about $0.22," while CEO Cooper added, "with more space, we should lease a little bit more, so it should be less than $0.22."
  • Srinivas, ATB Cormark: asked about rent differential on the 655 Bay backfill; CFO Jiang replied, "The rent that we're going to be collecting from the tenant is the same as what we were getting from ILAC on that individual space," and CEO Cooper added the tenant "took on just under another 10,000 feet" with a cash inducement.
  • Sam Damiani, TD Cowen: asked if the Sussex Center restructuring changed lender exposure; CEO Cooper answered, "It has no effect on the relationship between Dream Office REIT and the lender."
  • Damiani, TD Cowen: asked how Sussex will present in financials; CFO Jiang said, "the NOI on the top line will come down, but so will the interest expense, and it will be in the line called net income from JVs."
  • Mark Rothschild, Canaccord: asked about capital strategy and asset sales; CEO Cooper said, "I don't think at this point in our core portfolio in Toronto, we're looking to sell anything," adding, "the main driver we're looking at is to reduce our debt by EBITDA by growing our EBITDA."
  • Alex Leon, Desjardins: asked about ILAC backfill tenant types; CEO Cooper said 655 Bay is "very desirable to the province," while Kingsley Foris said, "the #1 user we would want in there... is another school," and "it's going to be more expensive to lease to -- if we don't lease to another school."
  • Leon, Desjardins: asked about incentives and refinancing; Foris said some higher incentives reflected older deals and that new-lease incentives have "come down," while CFO Jiang said refinancing assumptions are "5-year GLC, plus about somewhere between 150 to 200 basis points" and, "next year, we don't anticipate refinancing to be a headwind against FFO."

Sentiment Analysis

  • Analysts were slightly negative to neutral, repeatedly isolating ILAC downside and balance-sheet mechanics; questions focused on 2027 earnings sensitivity, JV reclassification implications, leasing incentives, and refinancing rates.
  • Management tone was slightly positive with specific caution around ILAC and transaction markets; CEO Cooper called ILAC a "punch to the gut," while CFO Jiang maintained guidance and said, "ILAC is expected to be a temporary setback."
  • Compared with the prior quarter, quarter-over-quarter sentiment comparisons were not possible because the previous-quarter transcript was not provided beyond a note stating it was unavailable.

Quarter-over-Quarter Comparison

  • A detailed comparison was not possible because the previous-quarter transcript content was not available in the prompt.
  • Within the current call, management explicitly referenced a guidance change driven by a post-quarter-end event: Toronto committed occupancy and in-place occupancy targets were revised downward following ILAC’s bankruptcy and lease disclaimer.

Risks and Concerns

  • Management identified tenant credit/event risk as the key near-term issue: "On September 18, International Language Academy of Canada, or ILAC, filed for bankruptcy and ceased operations" (CFO Siu-Ming Lau).
  • Foris quantified exposure from the unplanned vacancy returned: "approximately 80,000 square feet came back to us that was not in our plan," representing "about $4.3 million of annual gross rent beginning in Q4 of 2026."
  • Management indicated mitigation actions focused on rapid backfill and targeted marketing, including: "we signed a 53,000 square foot lease with a subtenant" (Kingsley Foris) and active outreach to school users and government-oriented demand for 655 Bay.

Final Takeaway

Management emphasized improving Toronto office fundamentals and stable 2026 NOI growth targets, while reframing ILAC’s bankruptcy as a near-term earnings and occupancy disruption that prompted lower year-end Toronto occupancy targets but did not change 2026 FFO guidance of $2.35 to $2.40 per unit. Executives highlighted quick backfill actions, ongoing leasing momentum (including narrowing committed-to-in-place occupancy), and continued focus on operating efficiency, refinancing execution, and rebuilding income and value at 425 Bloor and 655 Bay as re-leasing progresses.

data.title: S&P 500 reports weekly losses as technology rout weighs on markets
data.description:
Wall Street's major averages ended mixed on Friday, with the Nasdaq leading a recovery from its worst day in more than a year.

The benchmark S&P 500 (SP500) gained 0.3%, while the tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite finished advanced 1.1%, while the blue-chip Dow ended down 0.5%.

However, the S&P 500 also slipped 2.68% for the week.

From a sector-level perspective, six S&P 500 sectors ended the week in positive territory, while five finished in the red.

Seeking Alpha analyst Jack Bowman highlighted that this week was a wild week for stocks, and after the flush on Thursday, he is surprised that there are still gains to be had this week among sectors. 

Communication Services (XLC) and Consumer Discretionary (XLY) were the strongest performing sectors this week, with gains of 4.93% and 1.97%, respectively.

The analyst added that Communications and Consumer Discretionary were up despite the attribution from big tech firms like Alphabet, Meta, and Amazon. This showed a broadening of breadth on the week, which is a positive sign for our bull market, although it was not enough to save the index by a long shot. Big tech is just too concentrated.

Conversely, Energy (XLE) and Technology (XLK) posted the weakest weekly performances, falling 11.52% and 8.19%, respectively.

Bowman argued that we can see that the losers in the index were concentrated in technology and energy. Energy is responding to oil, which fell following the election on hopes of peace in the Middle East, although that is highly speculative.

“The big flush happened in tech as AI fears permeated the market. I am still bullish on big tech, as its valuations are now making it one of the cheapest in the market. And that's a considerable positive for tech investors that have wanted to load up but were cautious of valuations more broadly. I wouldn't be too concerned about the energy drop, as it has run up significantly and was overbought, so this could be a correction that preserves long-term momentum,” Bowman concluded.

Weekly S&P 500 sector performance:

  • Communication Services Select Sector SPDR Fund (XLC): +4.93%
  • Consumer Discretionary Select Sector SPDR Fund (XLY): +1.97%
  • Real Estate Select Sector SPDR Fund (XLRE): +1.95%
  • Financials Select Sector SPDR Fund (XLF): +1.20%
  • Consumer Staples Select Sector SPDR Fund (XLP): +0.76%
  • Health Care Select Sector SPDR Fund (XLV): +0.16%
  • Utilities Select Sector SPDR Fund (XLU): -0.69%
  • Materials Select Sector SPDR Fund (XLB): -1.46%
  • Industrials Select Sector SPDR Fund (XLI): -2.8%
  • Technology Select Sector SPDR Fund (XLK): -8.19%

data.title: U.S. indexes will hit new highs within three months, says SA analyst
data.description:
Seeking Alpha analyst Alex King of Cestrian Capital Research expects the major Wall Street indexes to hit new highs within the next three months.

“On Thursday this week, the AI trade nearly died but was immediately resuscitated by a never-ending slew of social media posts from politicians, financiers, and vendors about how everyone was still very committed to (i) AI and (ii) each other,” he said.

U.S. stocks pushed to recover from the ongoing technology selloff. The benchmark S&P 500 (SP500) ended +0.3%, while the tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite (COMP:IND) finished +1.1%, and the blue-chip Dow (DJI) closed -0.5%.

In addition, the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index (SOX) jumped 4.2%, while the Nasdaq 100 (QQQ) turned around and ended 1.5%.

Top semiconductors on Friday included Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing (TSM) +6.2%, Broadcom (AVGO) +0.6%, Micron Technology (MU) +5.2%, and Advanced Micro Devices (AMD) +10.6%.

“Frankenstein’s monster lives, and we believe it will march right back up the hill,” King said. “We anticipate new all-time highs in the equity indices within three months.”

data.title: SiriusPoint expects LPT to free over $200M and lift BSCR by around 20 points
data.description:
Earnings Call Insights: SiriusPoint (SPNT) Q3 2026

Management view

  • "Before I turn to the results, I want to welcome John Sauerland to our Board of Directors" (CEO & Director Scott Egan).

  • "The third quarter saw SiriusPoint deliver another strong performance with attractive underwriting margins, disciplined growth and returns above our 12% to 15% ROE target range" (CEO & Director Egan).

  • "The third quarter saw us deliver 20% growth in Insurance & Services and a Core Combined ratio of 90.1%" and "Our operating return on equity was 17.6%" (CEO & Director Egan).

  • "Today’s announcement [is] that we have entered into a loss portfolio transfer agreement with RiverStone that will substantially cover our remaining runoff exposures" and "following completion, our runoff exposures will be at de minimis levels" (CEO & Director Egan).

  • "[The LPT] frees up capital tied to these legacy reserves of over $200 million on completion and will increase our BSCR ratio by around 20 points" and "we will continue with our current buyback program" (CEO & Director Egan).

  • "Core gross written premium increased 14% to $991 million" and "Operating earnings per diluted share were $0.88" (CFO & Principal Accounting Officer James McKinney).

Outlook

  • "The transaction is subject to customary regulatory approvals" and "in an ideal world... we would get it done in Q4" and "Could it slip into Q1? Maybe" (CEO & Director Egan).

  • "We expect A&H premiums to return to low single-digit growth in the fourth quarter, while the pipeline entering 2027 remains encouraging" (CFO McKinney).

  • "Looking specifically to the fourth quarter, the nonrenewal of a FinPro program... is expected to result in Specialty P&C premiums being modestly lower year-over-year" and "We expect growth to resume in 2027" (CFO McKinney).

  • "The expected day 1 cost of the LPT is approximately $60 million" and "on a go-forward basis, we expect runoff losses to have a negligible impact" (CFO McKinney).

Financial results

  • "The core combined ratio was 90.1%, resulting in underwriting income of $76 million" and "Total investment income was $69 million, including $66 million of net investment income" (CFO McKinney).

  • "Net services fee income increased 21% year-over-year to $12 million" and "Operating net income was $103 million for the third quarter" (CFO McKinney).

  • "Diluted book value per share, excluding AOCI, increased by $0.73 during the quarter to $20.21" (CFO McKinney).

  • "Our estimated BSCR ratio was 232%" and "Following $27 million of common share repurchases in the quarter, $74 million remains under our authorization" (CFO McKinney).

Q&A

  • Michael Phillips, Oppenheimer: "Can you talk about [international A&H] a bit? Why was it exited...?" CEO & Director Egan: "For us, this was a performance reason. We weren't getting the traction that we wanted on the underwriting actions" and "it's not really a huge deal."

  • Michael Phillips, Oppenheimer: "I'm just looking... it's around $15 million, $16 million a year. Is that the right number to see?" CFO McKinney: "Yes... that's relatively the right number to consider." Phillips: "how long does this -- its business written before 2023?" CFO McKinney: "it basically has about a 3-year -- 2.5- to 3-year tail."

  • Michael Phillips, Oppenheimer: "does this recast say anything about the strategic rationale... the way you view reinsurance...?" CEO & Director Egan: "No, definitely not" and "I would not read that reinsurance in any way is not strategically important to the business."

  • Rowland Mayor, RBC Capital Markets: "Is there any further balance sheet optimization going forward?" CEO & Director Egan: "There's definitely a little bit more work that we probably do in the debt stack" and "99% of our efforts are in the go-forward potential of the business." CFO McKinney: "we... anticipate... less than kind of $100 million... deployed" in minority MGA elements and "we'll be able to... further optimize the debt stack of the company."

  • Rowland Mayor, RBC Capital Markets: "was the $27 million in the quarter impacted by the LPT?" and "Do you still expect to complete the authorization this year?" CFO McKinney: "The answer to both of those questions is yes" and "we intend to... restart the program."

  • Rowland Mayor, RBC Capital Markets: "I didn't see an expected close on the LPT." CEO & Director Egan: "We never try and forecast regulatory approval" and "in an ideal world... [Q4]... Could it slip into Q1? Maybe."

  • Andrew Andersen, Jefferies: "which businesses are contributing most to [the '27] pipeline...?" CEO & Director Egan: "I would probably highlight our MGA Global Programs business, as having a very strong and healthy pipeline" and "our A&H business, we're feeling quite upbeat going into 2027." CFO McKinney: "the mix shift... led to... the difference... between... gross written premium growth" and "as we go into 2027, there's an opportunity... you'll see more of our gross premium written... into the net written premium."

  • Andrew Andersen, Jefferies: "on employer stop loss... rate around 20%..." CEO & Director Egan: "Within U.S. Medical excess of loss, we are seeing rate expectations in excess of 20%" and "we are broadly carrying rate in line with claims inflation."

  • Timothy D'Agostino, B. Riley Securities: "Do you... potentially redomiciling...?" CEO & Director Egan: "in terms of our legal entity structure, that's something that we'll continue to evaluate" and "we're happy with the structure as it stands at the moment." CFO McKinney: "I would not overly focus on whether that is U.S. or Bermuda or another... the key element is what is the mix of the business going on."

  • Charles Peters, Raymond James: "Can you speak to... what lines of business you're getting favorable development from?" CEO & Director Egan: "we actually reserve above our price loss ratio" and "nothing is going to change in terms of our reserving approach." CFO McKinney: "we're seeing it favorable development across the portfolio."

Sentiment analysis

  • Analysts: slightly negative, with detailed probing on exits, LPT mechanics, capital actions, and structural questions such as domicile (e.g., "Do you -- like is there benefits to potentially redomiciling?").

  • Management: slightly positive and confident in prepared remarks and largely steady in Q&A, emphasizing volatility reduction and closure of legacy exposure (e.g., "Put simply, this transaction allows us to effectively close the chapter on the legacy book once and for all" (CEO & Director Egan)).

  • Versus last quarter: management tone stayed confident on discipline and cycle management, while analyst focus shifted from competition and product initiatives to the LPT’s practical impacts (timing, admin costs, repurchase resumption) and reporting/structure changes.

Quarter-over-quarter comparison

  • "Core Combined ratio" moved from "91.4%" in Q2 to "90.1%" in Q3 (CEO & Director Egan).

  • Operating return on equity increased from "13.8%" in Q2 to "17.6%" in Q3 (CEO & Director Egan).

  • Capital strength messaging shifted from "Our estimated BSCR ratio remains strong at 239%" in Q2 to "Our estimated BSCR ratio was 232%" in Q3 alongside a pro forma uplift expectation tied to the LPT (CFO McKinney).

  • Strategic emphasis broadened in Q3 to include "a loss portfolio transfer agreement with RiverStone" and a reporting change where "Accident & Health... becomes a stand-alone segment" beginning in Q4 (CEO & Director Egan).

Risks and concerns

  • "Pricing becomes more competitive in multiple lines of business" (CEO & Director Egan).

  • "Financial and professional lines remain competitive, particularly in D&O and professional liability" and "in Property Catastrophe Reinsurance... we expect continued pricing pressure" (CFO McKinney).

  • "Across both segments, losses recognized to date in relation to the Middle East conflict remain limited" (CFO McKinney).

Final takeaway

SiriusPoint’s management presented Q3 as another quarter of core underwriting and investment-driven returns above its 12% to 15% across-the-cycle ROE target, while highlighting a RiverStone loss portfolio transfer intended to reduce runoff volatility, move legacy exposures to “de minimis levels,” and (upon closing) free over $200 million of capital with an estimated BSCR benefit of around 20 points; management also outlined a forthcoming segment reporting change that will break out Accident & Health as a stand-alone segment beginning in Q4, alongside plans to resume share repurchases after the LPT announcement.
